audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-strict final stress, final stress) rests on the standard reference grammar of the language, Dayley's Tzutujil Grammar, which we hold (1981 dissertation scan) and whose section 1.3 states the rule verbatim as quoted, with an explicit rule V -> [+stress] / __ (C)# and the single native exception (unstressed adjectival connector -V, stress stays on the preceding stem vowel) plus Spanish loans. Two open items downloaded now from Ryan Bennett's site (2016 Mayan phonology survey, sec. 6.1; 2010 Tz'utujil stops study, p. 102) both restate 'final stress' / 'almost exceptionless word-final stress' from Dayley and cite no competing analysis; no instrumental stress study of Tz'utujil surfaced. The only housekeeping point is the locator: 'Dayley 1985:37' pairs the 1985 UCPL date with the 1981 dissertation page; UCPL 107 has the passage at p. 29 (per Bennett 2010). Suggest citi
